title: Grade 12 Mathematics - Introduction to Vectors and Linear Algebra
subject: Linear Algebra

transcript.text: Welcome to Grade 12 Linear Algebra. Today we introduce vectors, which are quantities that have both magnitude and direction.
A vector in 2D space is written as an ordered pair (x, y). For example, the vector (3, 4) points 3 units right and 4 units up. Its magnitude is sqrt(9 + 16) = 5.
To add two vectors, we add their components. If u = (2, 3) and v = (1, -1), then u + v = (3, 2). This is called component-wise addition.
Scalar multiplication scales a vector. Multiplying vector (2, 3) by scalar 3 gives (6, 9). This stretches the vector by a factor of 3 without changing its direction.
The dot product of two vectors u = (a, b) and v = (c, d) is u dot v = ac + bd. It is a scalar, not a vector. For u = (1, 2) and v = (3, 4), the dot product is 1*3 + 2*4 = 11.
Two vectors are orthogonal if their dot product is zero. For example, (1, 0) and (0, 1) have dot product 0, so they are perpendicular to each other.
A linear combination of vectors u and v is any expression of the form au + bv where a and b are scalars. The set of all such combinations is called the span of u and v.
Two vectors are linearly independent if neither is a scalar multiple of the other. In 2D, two linearly independent vectors span the entire plane.
